# A second SharedWorker window drops the replayed registerRemote

## Context

Measured 2026-09-04 09:12Z on engine `dev@35d468b51f` while running the multi-window reload rig for D#18224 (receipt: https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18224#discussioncomment-18284759). A `useSharedWorkers: true` app, one popup open, main window reloaded:

| page | `typeof Neo.worker.App` | remotes present |
|---|---|---|
| first connecting window | `'object'` | `createNeoInstance, destroyNeoInstance, fireEvent, getConfigs, getWorkerId, loadModule, moveComponent, setConfigs, setGlobalConfig` |
| the same window after `location.reload()` (worker kept alive by the popup) | **`'undefined'`** | none |

Two runs, same result. Observation and inference are separated below; the mechanism was then read at source.

#8339 (closed 2026-01-05, direct commit `c3a4e13cc9`, no PR) fixed exactly this symptom class — *"Remote Method Registration Missing for Secondary Windows in SharedWorker"* — by replaying every stored `registerRemote` to each newly connected port. The replay runs. The receiver drops it.

## The Problem

A window that connects to an already-running SharedWorker never gets the App worker's main-thread proxies. The first window gets them through the startup path; every later window — a second app window, or the first window after F5 — has `Neo.worker.App` undefined.

Consequence today: `src/worker/Manager.mjs:693` calls `Neo.worker.App.setGlobalConfig(config)` unguarded, so any global-config write issued from such a window throws; the remote methods documented as main-thread testing support (`moveComponent`, `destroyNeoInstance`, `createNeoInstance`) are unreachable from every window but the first. Nothing logs; the proxies are simply absent.

## The Architectural Reality

Three lines, read at `dev@35d468b51f`:

1. `src/worker/Base.mjs:209–210` (the #8339 replay, inside `onConnected`):
   ```js
   me.remotesToRegister.forEach(remote => {
       me.sendMessage(id, {action : 'registerRemote', ...remote})
   });
   ```
   `id` is the new **port id** (`Neo.getId('port')`).
2. `src/worker/Base.mjs:449` inside `sendMessage(dest, opts)`: `opts.destination = dest;` — so the replayed message reaches the right port but carries `destination: 'port-N'`.
3. `src/worker/mixin/RemoteMethodAccess.mjs:176`, the main thread's receiver: `if (remote.destination === Neo.workerId) { … }` — `Neo.workerId` is `'main'`, the message says `'port-N'`, the registration is silently ignored.

The startup path works because `core/Base.mjs#initRemote` → `Base.promiseRemotes(className, remote)` sends with `dest === 'main'`. The deprecation guard at `src/worker/Base.mjs:445` already exempts `registerRemote` from the "destination main is deprecated" warning — the intended shape of a registration message is `destination: 'main'` with a routing key, and the replay is the one sender that does not produce it.

`core/Base.mjs#initRemote` (~`:642–660`) is not at fault: it pushes `{className, methods: remote.main}` into `currentWorker.remotesToRegister` for every singleton in a SharedWorker, including `Neo.worker.App` itself. The list is right; the envelope is wrong.

## The Fix

`src/worker/Base.mjs:210` — send the replay addressed to `main` with the new port as the routing key, so the cascade documented at `:431–436` (direct dest → `opts.port` → `opts.windowId` → `opts.appName`) resolves the port while `destination` stays `'main'`:

```js
me.sendMessage('main', {action: 'registerRemote', port: id, ...remote})
```

`dest === 'main'` here is not the deprecated broadcast shape: `opts.port` is an explicit routing key, so the last-resort first-port fallback never runs, and the `registerRemote` exemption at `:445` keeps the console clean. The receiver's guard at `RemoteMethodAccess.mjs:176` is **kept** — it is what stops one window's registrations from landing in another.

Plus a witness on the worker side that pins the envelope, so the next refactor of `sendMessage` cannot silently re-break it.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.worker.App.<method>` proxies on the main thread of **every** connected window | the worker's `remote.main` config (`src/worker/App.mjs:40–51`) + `core/Base.mjs#initRemote` | present on the first window and on every window connecting to the running worker, incl. a reloaded one | none — absence is a `TypeError` at the call site | `src/worker/Base.mjs#onConnected` docblock names the replay contract | AC-1, AC-2 |
| `registerRemote` message envelope | `src/worker/Base.mjs#sendMessage` cascade docblock (`:431–436`) | `destination: 'main'`, `port: <new port id>` | — | `src/worker/Base.mjs#onConnected` docblock | AC-1 |
| duplicate `registerRemote` admission (`RemoteMethodAccess#onRegisterRemote`) | the `remote.origin !== 'main'` guard of `59a2a4010ce` (#698), narrowed rather than removed | a registration of the SAME endpoint — `className`, `method`, `origin` equal — is a no-op that keeps the existing proxy (the replay and the startup path both address the first window); any other occupant of the slot — a proxy for a different origin, or a local member — is a collision and throws | the throw: a wrong binding is never retained in silence | `onRegisterRemote` + `generateRemote` docblocks (`remoteProvenance`) | AC-3 + two negative unit controls (different origin, local member) |

## Decision Record impact

none — no ADR governs the worker message envelope; #8339's intent is restored, not changed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — unit witness on `Neo.worker.Base`: with `isSharedWorker` true and one `remotesToRegister` entry, a second `onConnected` posts a `registerRemote` whose `destination` is `'main'` and whose `port` is the new port's id; the message reaches only that port.
- [ ] AC-2 — a window that connects to a running SharedWorker has `typeof Neo.worker.App.moveComponent === 'function'` (whitebox or e2e arm on an existing multi-window fixture, e.g. the shared-worker child-app topology used by the `neuralLink` fixtures); the same arm reds at `dev@35d468b51f`.
- [ ] AC-3 — the first window's registration is unchanged: no `Duplicate remote method definition` throw, and `pkg[method] ??=` stays idempotent when both the startup path and the replay reach the same window.
- [ ] AC-4 — no `sendMessage destination "main" is deprecated` warning is emitted by the replay (the `:445` exemption covers it; the arm asserts the console).
- [ ] AC-5 — mutation-verified: reverting the one-line envelope change reds AC-1 and AC-2.

## Out of Scope

- The dock-layout rebind after reload (D#18224 Option G/H) — its live probe used the Neural Link precisely because this bug made the main-thread route unusable; the design does not depend on this fix.
- `Neo.appsByName[name]` retaining both Application generations after a reload (`controller/Application.mjs:84–85`, `component/Abstract.mjs:151` fallback) — separate lifecycle question, tracked on D#18224.
- Registration of **instance** remotes (`initRemote`'s ID-driven branch) — unaffected; they never use the broadcast path.

## Avoided Traps

- **Relaxing the receiver's guard** (`remote.destination === Neo.workerId`) to accept port-addressed registrations. The guard is what keeps a registration from landing in a window it was not sent to; the envelope is the thing to fix.
- **Sending with `dest === 'main'` and no routing key.** That hits the last-resort first-port fallback and registers the remotes into whichever window connected first — the misrouting class #17895 closed.
- **Re-registering at `afterConnect` for all ports.** Re-sending to already-served windows is harmless (`??=`) but noisy; the per-connection replay is the right hook, it only needs the right envelope.

## Related

- #8339 — the same symptom, fixed by direct commit `c3a4e13cc9` (2026-01-05): added `remotesToRegister` + the `onConnected` replay whose envelope this ticket corrects.
- #17895 — Dock FLIP messages omitted `windowId` and routed to the first port: the misrouting class the routing key avoids.
- #17899 — retiring the deprecated `'main'` destination; the `:445` exemption for `registerRemote` is its trace.
- #8366 — the earlier deprecation-warning fix for `registerRemote` messages.
- D#18224 — the multi-window transactions Discussion whose reload receipt surfaced this (comment `discussioncomment-18284759`).
